note: Attacker-controlled input from stdin/argv is accepted as a C string and its length is computed before any validation, establishing the propagation source.
The raw input is passed into the libidn2 conversion routine, which allocates and returns a transformed output buffer on success.
In decode mode, the same attacker-controlled string is routed into the punycode/Unicode decoder, exercising the vulnerable parsing path.
In default lookup/toASCII mode, the input is converted through the ASCII encoder path that ultimately consumes the malformed domain label.
Only successful conversions reach the sink, so the crafted payload must satisfy the parser enough to produce an output buffer and continue execution.

The memory-safety sink is the post-conversion heap deallocation/use of the conversion result; the crash is triggered by the malformed input driving the library into an invalid internal state before this point.
